diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For every $\delta \in [\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$ and every
    $x \in \RR^2$ with $I(\delta;\,x) = 0$, equality holds in
    Axiom~\ref{cond:monotonicity} if and only if $\nabla \risk(x) = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: At the included endpoint $\delta=\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta)=\eta$, the displayed remainder is identically zero for every boundary point, including nonstationary ones with $L_t\ne0$. Thus equality in one-step monotonicity does not occur only at stationary points, contrary to Axiom A6, so the claimed scalar example does not satisfy all the axioms as written.

failure_location.quote:
One verifies directly that Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} hold
with $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta) = \eta$ when $\eta <2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the stationarity axiom apply only for $\delta>\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta)$, or choose a threshold strictly larger than $\eta$ when invoking all axioms.
issues.overall_effect: The assertion that the paper's scalar certificate is an instance of the stated abstract framework is false at the threshold endpoint.
issues.title: The scalar certificate violates the stationarity axiom at the claimed threshold
issues.why_classification: Changing one endpoint convention locally restores compatibility without altering the certificate, dynamics, rates, or substantive convergence regimes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
It remains to explain why this local calculation determines the whole
state-dependent family on the nonterminal state space. The argument above shows
that, whenever a nonterminal level set contains an unbalanced global minimizer
$x_\ast=(a_\ast,b_\ast)$ with $a_\ast b_\ast=1$ and
$a_\ast\neq b_\ast$, the positive-definite quadratic form on that level set
is uniquely determined

Thus the unbalanced minimizers sweep out the full
nonterminal parameter range $(0,2)$. Consequently, every nonterminal level set
compatible with Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} is forced to coincide with the corresponding
level set of the family above.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only determines a quadratic form conditional on a particular level set containing an unbalanced minimizer; the axioms do not establish that every parameter value has such an intersection. More decisively, the axioms are invariant under nontrivial increasing reparameterizations. For example, from the displayed canonical family one may form \(\widetilde P(\delta)=P(\delta^2/2)\) on \((0,2]\). This has the same nested ellipsoids with a relabeled state, and it satisfies the structural axioms after correspondingly relabeling the admissible threshold (chosen strictly beyond the one-step equality endpoint), but it is not the formula asserted by the theorem at the same value of \(\delta\). No axiom normalizes the parameter to rule this out. The proof's claim that minimizers sweep the prescribed parameter range assumes precisely the parameter identification it is meant to prove.

failure_location.quote:
Assume the family $I(\delta;\,x) = x^\top P(\delta)\,x - 1$ satisfies
Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} for the scalar factorization
problem. Then $P(\delta)$ is uniquely determined for every
$\delta \in [\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must add and justify a parameter-normalization axiom, prove that every relevant level meets the unbalanced minimizer manifold, and redo the uniqueness argument, or materially weaken the conclusion to an appropriately proved equivalence class such as uniqueness up to reparameterization.
issues.overall_effect: The central exact uniqueness conclusion, and the claim that the stated structural axioms themselves select the specific scalar parameterization, are unsupported. Later uses of the explicit certificate remain usable when that family is chosen directly, but not as consequences of the uniqueness theorem.
issues.title: The axioms do not uniquely determine the parameterized quadratic family
issues.why_classification: As written, an entire family of counterexamples survives all structural requirements, and the proof also lacks the level-set intersection needed for its local calculation to cover all parameters. Repair requires new structural assumptions and argument, or abandonment of the advertised exact uniqueness claim.
